subject: Re: Aurora Financial — discount approval contingent on Compliance Pack scope
thread_body:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Aurora Financial — discount approval contingent on Compliance Pack scope

Team — need a quick alignment for Aurora Financial before I go back to Procurement today.

They’re requesting an additional 12% discount on the 12-month Dedicated commit. Procurement is tying approval to “security/compliance support included,” specifically:
- SOC 2 Type II report access + evidence request turnaround SLA
- Written confirmation on data use (“no training on customer prompts/data”) language
- Audit log retention > 90 days and export to their SIEM
- SSO/SAML + SCIM (they’re calling it “IdP lifecycle mgmt”)
- “Pen test results” (they asked for a full report; we should not provide that as-is)

I want to make sure we’re consistent with how we position the Enterprise Compliance Pack vs what’s in base, and ensure we’re not accidentally bundling gated evidence + extended support into the discount.

Proposal:
1) We approve the additional discount ONLY if they purchase the Enterprise Compliance Pack as a line item (not thrown in as free). 
2) Order Form language references the gated SOC 2 evidence process (NDA) and sets expectations on SLA.

Can you reply with:
- What we can commit to in the contract (and what we should keep as “available upon request under NDA”)?
- Any “do not say” reminders for this specific set of asks?

Attaching current Order Form draft + pricing approval request.

Thanks,
Stephanie

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Sales Readiness Lead
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 9:29 AM PST
Subject: Re: Aurora Financial — discount approval contingent on Compliance Pack scope

+1 to tying any extra discount to the Compliance Pack line item. We should not be “discounting by accident” by giving away evidence / SLAs as part of standard support.

Aisha/Naomi — can you confirm the safe commitments here (esp. audit log retention + evidence turnaround) and what we can *not* provide (pen test report, ISO language, etc.)?

Also reminder: they previously floated BAA/HIPAA language on the call notes — we should avoid implying we support HIPAA/BAA unless Legal explicitly approves.

Jordan

—
Jordan Blake
VP Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 10:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Aurora Financial — discount approval contingent on Compliance Pack scope

Here’s the capability/commitment view (contract-safe) based on current product behavior + our approved positioning:

OK to state (with correct caveats):
- SOC 2 Type II: “Report available under NDA via our evidence request process.” Do not attach the report to email / do not promise same-day delivery.
- Data use: We can use the approved “no training on customer data” definition (make sure it’s the exact phrasing from the kit; avoid broad statements like “never stored anywhere”).
- Audit logging: We support audit logs for console + API events, and export options (destination depends on deployment; generally S3/SIEM integration via customer pipeline). Phrase as “audit log export supported” and avoid enumerating fields unless using the standard list.
- SSO/SAML: supported for console access; SCIM provisioning supported for enterprise (tie to Compliance Pack if that’s how we’ve packaged it).

Not OK to commit / must avoid:
- Full penetration test report sharing. We can share an attestation letter / executive summary per the approved process, but not raw findings.
- “ISO 27001 certified.” We can say “alignment” or “controls map to ISO 27001 themes” if needed; do not claim certification.
- “Guaranteed data residency in any country.” Only state regions we currently support and Private/VPC options (no roadmap).

On the SLA: we need Aisha/GRC to confirm what we’re currently comfortable committing to (e.g., 5 business days for evidence requests under NDA). I’d keep it “target response time” unless Aisha explicitly wants it in the Order Form.

Naomi

—
Naomi Feldman
Product Security PM
Redwood Inference

From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 10:41 AM PST
Subject: Re: Aurora Financial — discount approval contingent on Compliance Pack scope

Agree with the approach: discount is contingent on Compliance Pack being purchased as a separate SKU/line item.

Security/compliance specifics:
1) SOC 2 Type II report: “available under NDA through our evidence request process.” Do not put the report itself in a deal room without GRC tracking.
2) Pen test: we do not provide full reports. Approved alternative: “We conduct regular third-party penetration testing; an attestation letter or executive summary may be provided under NDA upon request.”
3) Evidence turnaround: we can commit to a standard response SLA ONLY as part of the Compliance Pack. For most requests, we can target 5 business days once NDA is in place and the request is complete. Anything faster is an escalation.
4) Avoid absolute claims: no “we never retain any data” language. Stick to the retention/residency wording from the kit.

Contract/process reminder: If Procurement asks for bespoke breach notification timelines or security addendum edits, loop Legal. We should not negotiate those in Sales email.

Aisha

—
Dr. Aisha Rahman
Chief Information Security Officer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Aurora Financial — discount approval contingent on Compliance Pack scope

Sharing copy you can paste back to Procurement (aligned to the enablement kit language). Feel free to use verbatim:

“Redwood offers an Enterprise Compliance Pack that includes (i) guided security review support, (ii) accelerated compliance evidence request handling (SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA), and (iii) enhanced audit logging and retention options (deployment-mode dependent). Access to certain compliance artifacts is gated via NDA and our evidence request workflow.”

For the discount framing:
- “We can extend the additional discount contingent on packaging the Enterprise Compliance Pack as part of the agreement. This ensures the right SLAs and support resources are allocated to meet your review timeline.”

If they push on ISO:
- “Redwood maintains a mature security program and can provide documentation mapping our controls to ISO 27001 themes upon request; Redwood does not represent itself as ISO 27001 certified unless explicitly stated in a current certificate.”

Stephanie — if you want, I can also send you the latest one-pager positioning blurb so Procurement sees it as a standard offering vs a one-off concession.

Camila

—
Camila Reyes
Product Marketing
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 1:26 PM PST
Subject: Re: Aurora Financial — discount approval contingent on Compliance Pack scope

Super helpful, thank you.

Before I send the updated terms back, two quick confirmations so we stay tight:

1) Evidence SLA wording — are we comfortable putting “5 business days after NDA + complete request” directly in the Order Form as the Compliance Pack SLA, or should we keep it as “target” language in email only?

2) Audit log retention — I’m planning to say:
- “Audit log retention is configurable; extended retention beyond standard defaults is available with enterprise/compliance packaging.”

Is that accurate enough without getting into 90/180/365 specifics?

Draft response to Aurora Procurement (for visibility):

- Additional 12% discount approved contingent on adding Enterprise Compliance Pack as a separate line item.
- Compliance Pack includes: guided security review support, accelerated evidence handling (SOC 2 Type II report under NDA), and enhanced audit logging/retention options.
- Pen test: attestation letter / exec summary under NDA; no full report.

I’ll hold until I get a quick yes/no on the SLA phrasing.

Stephanie

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 5:48 PM PST
Subject: Re: Aurora Financial — discount approval contingent on Compliance Pack scope

1) SLA phrasing: recommend we keep the Order Form language as “standard response SLA for evidence requests as part of the Compliance Pack (details in the Evidence Request Playbook)” and keep “5 business days after NDA + complete request” in an email / SOW. That gives us room for edge cases (incomplete request, non-standard artifacts, etc.). If Procurement insists on hard SLA in the Order Form, we should route to Aisha for explicit sign-off.

2) Audit log retention: your wording is good. If they demand specifics, the safest version is:
- Hosted/Dedicated: extended retention options are available for audit logs (up to 12 months depending on plan/config).
- Private: retention is customer-configurable (they control storage/retention policies), with Redwood providing the audit event stream.

Also +1 to not mentioning 90/180/365 unless you’re quoting the current packaged defaults verbatim from the standard answers doc.

Naomi
